title: Unlimited Approval
intro: Chapter 5. These scams don't ask for your phrase. They ask for one click.
Toddy found a "free mint" site. The wallet pops up asking to approve something.
Read what the pop-up really allows.

screen.title: Allow access to your ZLV?
screen.context: You clicked "Mint for free" on a site you found in a group chat.

note.text: Hedrio: This lets the site move your ZLV at any time, without asking again.

amount.label: Unlimited amount
amount.lens: UNLIMITED: they could take all your ZLV, now or later.
amount.why: A free mint never needs permission to spend all your coins.

spender.label: Unknown spender
spender.lens: An unknown contract gets the permission.
spender.why: Approvals hand control to whoever owns that contract.

site.label: Random mint site
site.lens: A site from a group chat, not an official link.
site.why: Drainer sites pose as free mints and airdrops.

warning.label: Wallet warning
warning.lens: Your wallet itself is warning you.
warning.why: Read wallet warnings. They exist for this exact trick.

free.label: Free mint
free.why: Free mints exist. The approval is the problem, not the price.

actions.label: Reject, and look for the project's official mint link

block_report.line: Rejected and reported. The wallet now flags that site for everyone.

verify.line: The real project had no free mint at all. Rejecting saved everything.

go_ahead.line: Days later, every ZLV quietly left the wallet. The approval let it happen.

what_if.go_ahead: "UNLIMITED" plus an unknown spender was the moment to reject.

golden_rule: Read every wallet pop-up. Never approve "unlimited" spending for a site you don't fully trust.

quick_check.q: A free mint asks for UNLIMITED access to your coins. What do you do?
quick_check.explain: Drainers can act the moment you approve. "Later" may be too late.

rows.v: A group chat, not an official link
